rows.title: Will Lamont replace all vanishing SNAP benefits? He won’t say
rows.standfirst: The Connecticut General Assembly could give the governor a lot of flexibility in deciding when to release funds for SNAP and how much.

rows.title: Lamont pledges to restart SNAP benefits in days – even if CT pays
rows.standfirst: SNAP benefits will be available in next few days with CT funds, possibly by Saturday, but the USDA also plans to restart payments soon.

rows.title: CT plans $500M in relief for federal programs, but questions remain
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont outlined plans to protect federal human service programs. But it remained unclear how far Connecticut will spread the money.

rows.title: Swelling CT revenues could intensify response to federal cuts
rows.standfirst: The CT revenue projections — about $1.1 billion in extra revenue this fiscal year — likely will expand calls for more state tax cuts.

rows.title: CT House adopts relief fund to bolster federal programs
rows.standfirst: Creating the emergency fund could push CT over its budgetary spending cap, so the measure had to pass with at least a 60% majority. It did.

rows.title: CT Senate gives final approval to emergency human services fund
rows.standfirst: The CT Senate voted 27-8 to designate $500 million to potentially backfill federal cuts to nutrition and other human service programs.

rows.title: CT 211 Infoline seeks first funding hike in 15 years
rows.standfirst: The human services 211 lifeline fields thousands of inquiries a day on average, and demand is expected to grow with federal cutbacks.

rows.title: Jeffrey Beckham, who stabilized CT budget office, to step down next month
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont to tap Josh Wojcik, key health policy leader in the state comptroller’s office, to lead the Office of Policy and Management.

rows.title: Lamont taps Jeffrey Beckham to become Superior Court judge
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont announced he will nominate his departing budget director, Jeffrey Beckham of Tolland, to become a CT Superior Court judge.

rows.title: Surging CT surplus approaches $2 billion
rows.standfirst: The sharpest growth comes in tax receipts tied to quarterly filings, dominated by capital gains and other investment-related earnings.

rows.title: CT begins broader debate over vanishing federal funds
rows.standfirst: State leaders now must decide whether CT should indefinitely dedicate millions to reverse gaps created by retreating federal funding.
